transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been seeing and hearing things at work and at home that no one else seems to notice, and it’s starting to scare me. I don't really know how to explain it, but it's making it very hard to function right now.
Did these experiences start after using alcohol, drugs, or new medications, or after any recent illness or head injury? If so, which one came first?

No, I haven't had any head injuries, illnesses, or used any drugs, alcohol, or new medications. These experiences actually started building up after a really stressful reorganization at my job instead.

How long have these hallucinations and unusual experiences been going on in total—days, weeks, or months? Have there been any periods of several days when you also felt unusually high-energy, needed much less sleep, or felt extremely up or irritable?

The whispers and shadows have been happening steadily for about ten months now, although things first started changing after the reorganization fifteen months ago. And yes, for almost the past year, I’ve had these long stretches where I feel incredibly revved up, sleep only a couple of hours a night, and swing between feeling on top of the world and being extremely snappy.

During those 10 months of hearing whispers and seeing shadows, were there ever at least 2 weeks when the hallucinations continued even though you were not feeling unusually high-energy, euphoric, or irritable? Or do the hallucinations only happen during those revved-up mood periods?

Yes, there was a stretch earlier this year for at least a couple of weeks where my mood felt completely neutral and I wasn't revved up at all, but the whispers and shadows didn't stop. Even during that flat period, I was still hearing those voices and believing the office emails were coded messages about me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory and visual hallucinations, delusion-like belief that office emails were coded messages about them) occurring for about 10 months, along with prolonged manic symptoms (high energy, markedly decreased need for sleep, euphoric/irritable mood). Crucially, psychotic symptoms persisted for at least 2 weeks during a neutral mood period, supporting schizoaffective disorder, manic type rather than a primary bipolar disorder with psychotic features. Substance/medication and medical causes were denied.
